title: A kinetic model of electron transfer at the electrode-electrolyte interface: Statistical mechanics and electrochemical aspects
authors: Diego Veloza-Diaz, Robinson Cortes-Huerto, Pietro Ballone, Nancy C. Forero-Martinez
abstract: A new simulation approach ({\it J. Chem. Phys.} {\bf 163}, 164113), based on the seamless combination of the electron transfer at the electrode/electrolyte interface with the charge and mass transport in electrolyte solutions, holds the promise to advance the comprehensive modeling of basic electrochemical devices such as electrolytic cells and batteries. The underlying model also includes a fully consistent treatment of structural, thermodynamic and statistical properties of the electrical double-layer at non-ideal electron-conducting interfaces. As a result, subtle aspects such as Tafel and Butler-Volmer equations, the overpotential concept, as well as (stationary) non-equilibrium features such as the entropy production, arise naturally from the model, with a minimum of ad-hoc assumptions and elaborations of the simulation results. We illustrate these aspects for a simple model of electrochemical interface, and discuss further improvements of the method meant to enhance its ability to model systems and phenomena of interest for electrochemistry. One such improvement, concerning the effect of fluctuating electric fields on the electron transfer rate, is explicitly developed.
summary: This work presents a new simulation framework to model electron transfer at electrochemical interfaces, integrating electronic and ionic transport. By combining Monte Carlo and kinetic simulations, the model naturally yields fundamental electrochemical laws like the Butler-Volmer equation. This advances the field by providing a statistically rigorous approach to non-equilibrium electrochemistry.
main_problem: Developing a comprehensive theoretical/computational model for electron transfer at the electrode-electrolyte interface by consistently coupling electronic and ionic transport.
main_result: The new model naturally derives key electrochemical concepts like Tafel and Butler-Volmer equations and entropy production with minimal ad-hoc assumptions.
method: A novel simulation approach combining Grand-Canonical Monte Carlo (GC-MC) for electrolyte state fixing with kinetic simulations for electron transfer.
model_or_system: The system is an electrode/electrolyte interface, modeled using a primitive electrolyte (hard-sphere plus Coulomb interaction) coupled to quantum mechanical charge transfer kinetics.
key_observables: Tafel and Butler-Volmer equations, overpotential, entropy production, radial electric current density j_r(R_e), and probability distribution P(E_r) of the radial field.
important_parameters: Surface charge density ($\sigma_e$), ionic strength, diffusion constant, and the intrinsic rate of electron transfer.
main_assumptions: The initial model assumes a rigid electrode and a primitive electrolyte; later extensions aim to incorporate fluctuating electric fields and feedback mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the half-cell model for reduction/oxidation, and show the dependence of overpotential ($\Delta V$) on current density ($j_r$) at constant surface charge ($\sigma_e$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the basic model yielding fundamental electrochemical concepts, and then systematically extends the model's realism by incorporating complex feedback mechanisms, such as fluctuating electric fields affecting the charge transfer rate.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation of non-equilibrium thermodynamics (entropy production) and the coupling of quantum charge transfer rates to classical ionic dynamics provides a powerful framework for open quantum systems modeling.
